title: Predator and prey
experiment: Switching on a prey carrying capacity turns the closed predator–prey cycles of §2 into a spiral toward equilibrium, which is the claim of §3.
archetype_reason: Two populations change continuously under the ODEs written in §1.

source.quote: Prey x grow at rate α and are eaten at rate βxy
predators y gain δxy and die at rate γ
prey sit at the equilibrium x* = γ/δ, whatever the starting point.
Give prey a carrying capacity K, so they grow as αx(1 − x/K), and the cycles damp out

metrics.name: amp_ratio
metrics.label: swing ratio
metrics.meaning: prey swing (max − min) over the last quarter of the run divided by the swing over the first quarter

metrics.name: mean_prey
metrics.label: mean prey
metrics.meaning: time average of prey over the whole run

reproduce.claim: Without a carrying capacity the swings keep their size and prey average x* = γ/δ = 10.

source.quote: every orbit is closed and the swings never shrink. Averaged over the cycles, prey sit at the equilibrium x* = γ/δ

contrast.claim: With a carrying capacity the late swings shrink to under a third of the cycling case.

source.quote: the cycles damp out: the populations spiral into the equilibrium.
